newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly up on Monday, boosted by a surge on Shanghai's domestic A share market, which attracted funds from the repo market, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract rose to 11.20 percent from 10.00 percent last Friday.
Turnover surged to 9.06 million lots from 5.53 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
"Active trading on the A share market was the major factor for today's rises," a trader said. Shanghai's A share index surged 9.94 percent on year-high volume of 16.7 billion yuan.
"The contracts are likely to continue rising in the next few days due to a strong A share market," said a second trader.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly down on institutional selling, traders said. Total volume of the nine-contract market was 1.07 million lots, from 1.34 million.
The most active three-year bond that matures in 1999 fell to 101.50 yuan from 101.64 yuan.

"Institutions sold on the market today on expectations that the contracts would continue to fall," said one trader. The market has been on a downtrend for months partly because liquidity has been flowing to the surging A share markets.
